title: 2D MultiMesh draws nothing on PowerVR DXT (GL Compatibility) when instance count is >256 and not a power of two
body:
﻿### Tested versions

4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4]

### System information

Google Pixel 10 Pro XL (mustang), Android 16, PowerVR D-Series DXT-48-1536, OpenGL ES 3.2 build 25.1@6794074, gl_compatibility renderer. Not reproducible on desktop NVIDIA (OpenGL Compatibility) with identical scenes - device-specific.

### Issue description

On this driver, a `MultiMeshInstance2D` draw (TRANSFORM_2D + colors + custom data, ShaderMaterial canvas_item shader) is invisible whenever the drawn instance count is **greater than 256 and not an exact power of two**. No GL errors, no warnings; non-instanced canvas items in the same frame render normally. Measured by frame readback across a count sweep on device:

| count | result | | count | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 / 200 / 256 | visible | | 257 / 300 / 511 | black |
| 512 | visible | | 513 / 735 / 1023 | black |
| 1024 / 2048 / 4096 | visible | | 1025 / 1536 / 2047 / 2049 / 3072 / 4095 / 4097 / 5120 | black |

No latching: the same MultiMesh flips visible/black purely by changing `visible_instance_count` between good/bad values, with identical instance content - so this is not the stale-AABB canvas culling of #119151 (same content, same AABB, only the count changes).

Suspected mechanism: `RasterizerCanvasGLES3::_enable_attributes()` binds the per-item batch attributes (locations 8-15) with `glVertexAttribDivisor(i, p_rate)` where `p_rate == instance_count` for multimesh draws (rasterizer_canvas_gles3.cpp, `_render_batch()` TYPE_MULTIMESH). Divisor = count keeps `floor(gl_InstanceID / divisor) == 0` so one InstanceData record serves the whole draw - but large non-power-of-two divisor values appear to be mishandled by this driver, leaving the item transform/modulate attributes reading garbage (world transform collapses / modulate zero), so the whole draw disappears. Powers of two presumably hit a native shift path. GLES 3.2 permits arbitrary divisors, matching the absence of errors. The 3D path (divisor 1) is unaffected, which fits this being 2D-only.

App-level workaround that holds: keep `instance_count` a power of two and never draw a non-pow2 count (pad with fully transparent instances).

Related: #113911 (GPU particles crash on the same GPU + renderer, closed as driver-side) - same driver family misbehaving under the GLES3 paths. Godot 4.5.2 added all PowerVR GPUs to the transform-feedback shader-cache ban list, so there is precedent for PowerVR-specific workarounds.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a MultiMeshInstance2D (TRANSFORM_2D, use_colors, use_custom_data), fill N instances on screen, set `visible_instance_count` to values from the table above; read back the viewport (or just look at the screen).

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Standalone public MRP: https://github.com/ElodinLaarz/godot-mm2d-count-mrp

One MultiMeshInstance2D, buffer written once (static colored-quad grid, generous `custom_aabb` so #119151's stale cull rect is excluded); the sweep flips only `visible_instance_count` and readback-verdicts each count (`[mrp]` lines, desktop exits non-zero if any count went black). Fresh output from the affected device:

```
[mrp] count  256: VISIBLE (64/64 sampled instance centers lit)
[mrp] count  257: BLACK (0/64 sampled instance centers lit)
[mrp] count  512: VISIBLE (64/64 sampled instance centers lit)
[mrp] count  513: BLACK (0/64 sampled instance centers lit)
[mrp] count 1024: VISIBLE (64/64 sampled instance centers lit)
[mrp] count 1025: BLACK (0/64 sampled instance centers lit)
[mrp] summary: 14/21 counts invisible: [257, 300, 511, 513, 735, 1023, 1025, 1536, 2047, 2049, 3072, 4095, 4097, 5120]
```

Desktop control (NVIDIA, GL Compatibility and Forward+): all 21 counts VISIBLE.
